title: Boulegeris Investments Inc. Sells 14,304 Shares of Apple Inc. (AAPL)
text:
Tweet
Boulegeris Investments Inc. lowered its position in shares of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 28.7% in the first quarter, according to its most recent Form 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The fund owned 35,507 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 14,304 shares during the quarter. Apple makes up about 3.3% of Boulegeris Investments Inc.’s holdings, making the stock its 6th largest holding. Boulegeris Investments Inc.’s holdings in Apple were worth $5,957,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Several other institutional investors have also recently made changes to their positions in AAPL. Stevens Capital Management LP purchased a new stake in shares of Apple in the first quarter valued at approximately $1,159,000. Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management grew its position in shares of Apple by 11.4% in the first quarter. Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management now owns 81,653 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $13,699,000 after purchasing an additional 8,336 shares in the last quarter. Newport Wealth Strategies Inc. grew its position in shares of Apple by 6.4% in the first quarter. Newport Wealth Strategies Inc. now owns 17,203 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $2,886,000 after purchasing an additional 1,037 shares in the last quarter. Marcus Capital LLC grew its position in shares of Apple by 6.8% in the first quarter. Marcus Capital LLC now owns 4,342 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $729,000 after purchasing an additional 275 shares in the last quarter. Finally, O Shaughnessy Asset Management LLC grew its position in shares of Apple by 9.1% in the first quarter. O Shaughnessy Asset Management LLC now owns 138,708 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $23,273,000 after purchasing an additional 11,547 shares in the last quarter. 58.39% of the stock is owned by institutional investors and hedge funds. In other news, insider Angela J. Ahrendts sold 38,228 shares of the stock in a transaction on Friday, May 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $176.54, for a total value of $6,748,771.12. Following the sale, the insider now directly owns 90,967 shares in the company, valued at $16,059,314.18. The sale was disclosed in a legal filing with the SEC, which can be accessed through this hyperlink . Also, insider Luca Maestri sold 4,769 shares of the stock in a transaction on Friday, June 1st. The shares were sold at an average price of $189.54, for a total value of $903,916.26. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now owns 68,044 shares in the company, valued at $12,897,059.76. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last quarter, insiders sold 168,738 shares of company stock worth $31,247,951. Insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock. Apple opened at $201.50 on Thursday, according to MarketBeat.com . Apple Inc. has a 52 week low of $149.16 and a 52 week high of $201.76. The firm has a market cap of $963.61 billion, a PE ratio of 21.88, a PEG ratio of 1.53 and a beta of 1.24. The company has a quick ratio of 1.37, a current ratio of 1.46 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, July 31st. The iPhone maker reported $2.34 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $2.18 by $0.16. The business had revenue of $53.27 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $52.43 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The company’s revenue for the quarter was up 17.3% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same period last year, the firm earned $1.67 earnings per share. equities research analysts predict that Apple Inc. will post 11.41 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
Apple announced that its board has authorized a share buyback plan on Tuesday, May 1st that allows the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This repurchase authorization allows the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock repurchase plans are usually an indication that the company’s board of directors believes its shares are undervalued.
The business also recently disclosed a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, August 16th. Stockholders of record on Monday, August 13th will be paid a $0.73 dividend. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a dividend yield of 1.45%. The ex-dividend date of this dividend is Friday, August 10th. Apple’s payout ratio is currently 31.70%.
A number of equities research analysts have recently issued reports on the company. Guggenheim restated a “buy” rating and issued a $235.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research report on Wednesday. Rosenblatt Securities set a $200.00 price target on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research report on Wednesday. Macquarie set a $214.00 price target on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research report on Wednesday. Sanford C. Bernstein set a $200.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research report on Wednesday. Finally, Atlantic Securities set a $205.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research report on Wednesday. One equities research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, fifteen have issued a hold rating, thirty-four have issued a buy rating and two have given a strong buy rating to the stock. The stock currently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average target price of $224.48.
About Apple
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. The company also sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.
